rounds.text: The bull case of a cheap multiple is undermined by a severe long-term decay in earning power, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth rate of -2% [E18]. This historical destruction of value is further highlighted by a decade-long median return on equity of just 7% and a 5-year median ROE of 8% [E26, E27]. Beneath recent short-term acceleration, the core business engine has contracted significantly, demonstrated by a poor sales growth of -14.7% over the past five years [E59]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero return on their capital via cash distributions, as evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong profit growth of 66% compounded over 5 years [E19].

Conceded: 10-year compounded profit growth is -2% [E18] and 5-year sales growth is -14.7% [E59]. However, pointing to long-term decay ignores a massive structural turnaround where 5-year compounded profit growth has surged to 66% [E19], 3-year growth sits at 22% [E20], and trailing twelve-month growth has accelerated to 48% [E21], outpacing the sector median profit growth of 20.6% [E70]. This acceleration is fundamentals-led, with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 77% [E53]. The historical drag on return on equity is steadily improving rather than permanent, climbing from a 10-year median of 7% [E26] up to a current 11.0% [E13] (or 10.37% against sector benchmarks [E9]), demonstrating that recent profitability is robustly outperforming historical medians. Finally, the absence of dividends [E4] is not value destruction when earnings are compounding rapidly at 66% over 5 years [E19] and driving an exceptionally low P/E of 5.86x [E1].

Conceded: 5-year compounded profit growth is 66% [E19] and trailing twelve-month growth is 48% [E21]. However, this recent acceleration obscures a severe structural decay in top-line operations, evidenced by a poor sales growth of -14.7% over the past five years [E59] and a 10-year compounded profit growth of -2% [E18]. The bull points to an improving return on equity reaching 11.0% [E13], but glosses over the reality that the low return on equity over the last 3 years averages just 8.68% [E60], with a 10-year median stuck at a meager 7% [E26]. While the bull dismisses the absence of dividends [E4], a 0.00% payout combined with the stock sitting only 30% of the way up its 52-week range [E5] shows that the market refuses to price in these accelerating earnings as a sustainable rerating catalyst.
